overview: This 634-page file traces U.S. occupation control of Japanese fisheries, especially the disputed 1946–47 Antarctic whaling expedition. Diplomatic correspondence records Allied objections, food-supply arguments, inspection plans, vessel flags, and access to fishing grounds. Historical Antarctic catch maps and detailed fleet and coastal catch reports accompany smaller files on seed oysters, cultured pearls, agar, and an investigation into private pearl trading during an official mission.
interest: Combines diplomatic disputes with operational fleet records and historical catch maps, revealing how occupation authorities managed Japan’s marine industries.
